facts.raw_span: sudden-onset chest pain
history of diabetes
paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
Normal sinus rhythm
up to 2.0-mm ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9
1.0-mm to 2.0-mm downward-sloping ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4
R/S greater than 1 in leads V1-V2
Initial high-sensitive troponin T level: 0.309 ng/mL
thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion
blood pressure fell to 60/40 mm Hg

concepts.why: The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain, had ST-segment elevation in multiple leads, and an elevated troponin T level, all of which are indicative of an acute myocardial infarction.
The patient's blood pressure fell to 60/40 mm Hg, which is a sign of cardiogenic shock, and the presence of an acute myocardial infarction and elevated troponin T level support this diagnosis.
The patient had a pericardial effusion as shown by the computer tomography angiography, which is a sign of pericardial disease.

concepts.preferred_label: Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response
concepts.why: The patient has a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, which is a type of arrhythmic disorder.
It explains the ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4 and R/S greater than 1 in leads V1-V2, which are indicative of inferior wall ischemia.
It explains the subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9, which is indicative of posterior wall ischemia.

rationales.F01: Sudden-onset chest pain is a classic symptom of acute myocardial infarction.
rationales.F03: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is a risk factor for atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.
rationales.F04: Normal sinus rhythm rules out atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.
rationales.F05: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF is indicative of inferior wall myocardial infarction.
rationales.F06: ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9 is indicative of posterior wall myocardial infarction.
rationales.F09: Elevated troponin levels are a strong indicator of acute myocardial infarction.
rationales.F10: Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery is a common cause of acute myocardial infarction.
rationales.F11: Contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion is indicative of pericardial effusion.
rationales.F12: Hypotension is a symptom of cardiogenic shock.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's ECG findings, including ST-segment elevation in multiple leads and high-sensitive troponin T level, along with thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery, strongly support acute myocardial infarction as the primary diagnosis.
